I'll solve this directly using the modular transformation properties of the Dedekind eta function.

## Solution

**Setup.** Recall $\phi(q) = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty}(1-q^n) = q^{-1/24}\eta(\tau)$, where $q = e^{2\pi i\tau}$ and $\eta(\tau) = q^{1/24}\prod_{n\geq 1}(1-q^n)$ is the Dedekind eta function. We approach $q\to 1$ radially, taking $\tau = it$ with $t\to 0^+$ (so $q = e^{-2\pi t}\to 1^-$).

**Asymptotic of $\eta$ near the cusp.** The modular transformation is
$$\eta(-1/\tau) = \sqrt{-i\tau}\,\eta(\tau).$$
For $\tau = it$ with $t\to 0^+$: $-1/\tau = i/t\to i\infty$, and $\eta(i/t) = e^{-\pi/(12t)}\prod_{n\geq 1}(1-e^{-2\pi n/t}) \sim e^{-\pi/(12t)}$. Also $\sqrt{-i\tau}=\sqrt{-i\cdot it}=\sqrt{t}$. Hence
$$\eta(it) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\,e^{-\pi/(12t)}, \qquad t\to 0^+.$$

**Asymptotic of $\phi(q)$.** Since $\phi(q) = q^{-1/24}\eta(\tau) = e^{\pi t/12}\eta(it)$,
$$\phi(q) \sim e^{\pi t/12}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\,e^{-\pi/(12t)} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\,e^{\pi t/12 - \pi/(12t)}.$$

**Asymptotic of $\phi(q^5)$.** Here $q^5 = e^{-10\pi t}$, corresponding to $\tau' = 5it$ (i.e. $t\mapsto 5t$). Thus
$$\phi(q^5) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{5t}}\,e^{5\pi t/12 - \pi/(60t)}.$$

**Forming the ratio.**
$$\phi^5(q) \sim t^{-5/2}\,e^{5\pi t/12 - 5\pi/(12t)},$$
so
$$\frac{\phi^5(q)}{\phi(q^5)} \sim \frac{t^{-5/2}\,e^{5\pi t/12 - 5\pi/(12t)}}{(5t)^{-1/2}\,e^{5\pi t/12 - \pi/(60t)}} = \sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,\exp\!\Big(\!-\tfrac{5\pi}{12t}+\tfrac{\pi}{60t}\Big).$$

Combining the exponents: $-\tfrac{5}{12}+\tfrac{1}{60} = \tfrac{-25+1}{60} = -\tfrac{24}{60} = -\tfrac{2}{5}$, giving
$$\frac{\phi^5(q)}{\phi(q^5)} \sim \sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,e^{-2\pi/(5t)}.$$

**Taking the limit.** As $t\to 0^+$, the factor $e^{-2\pi/(5t)}$ decays to $0$ exponentially fast, while $t^{-2}$ grows only polynomially. Exponential decay dominates polynomial growth, so
$$\lim_{t\to 0^+}\sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,e^{-2\pi/(5t)} = 0.$$

Since the radial approach $q\to 1^-$ yields $0$, and the eta function's behavior is governed by the same cusp asymptotics for any approach within the unit disk to the cusp $q=1$,

$$\boxed{\lim_{q\to 1}\frac{\phi^5(q)}{\phi(q^5)} = 0.}$$
